deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 13% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.9% = 10-year Treasury 4.9% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 83% last year; 110%/yr over 3 years — the market expects a slowdown from its recent pace.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 81% (3 years ago 47%, rising) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $81 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 84% (3 years ago 38%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $3.2B, up 68% from a year ago — about 1% of the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $6.4B, up 215% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Receivables (money customers still owe) up 127% vs quarterly sales up 106% (days to collect 54 → 60). Customers may be paying more slowly, or sales were pulled forward.

connects.text: AI spending: big cloud companies' capital spending is up 88% from a year ago → supports demand for NVDA.
US export controls on advanced chips: “NVIDIA Board of Directors Establishes National Security and Export Control Oversight…”.
GOOGL (customer): “Intensifying AI rout wipes out Nasdaq's 2026 gains. Alphabet is a tech bright spot” → a stronger customer usually means more orders for NVDA.
ORCL (customer): “Big bets against AI debt, from CoreWeave to Oracle and the Mag 7, could soon hit the ETF…” → a weaker customer can mean fewer orders for NVDA.

connects_more.text: NBIS (customer): “Nebius falls 10% as company expects increased 2026 capex spend, issues weak outlook” → its spending plans decide how much it buys from NVDA.
Interest rates: next jobs report on Dec 4 → higher rates weigh most on highly valued stocks.
MU (supplier) reports Dec 17: a read-across for NVDA's supply and costs.
DELL (customer) reports Nov 24: a read-across for NVDA's demand.
TSM (supplier): TSMC fabricates NVIDIA GPUs; NVIDIA 10-K names TSMC as a key foundry partner.
MSFT (customer): Azure is a major buyer of NVIDIA data-center GPUs.
AMZN (customer): AWS is a major buyer of NVIDIA data-center GPUs.
META (customer): Meta has publicly described large NVIDIA GPU clusters.
AMD (rival): Both 10-Ks name each other as competitors in GPUs/accelerators.
CRWV (customer): CoreWeave S-1 describes dependence on NVIDIA GPUs; NVIDIA is also an investor.
SMCI (customer): Supermicro builds NVIDIA GPU servers; depends on GPU allocation.
VRT (partner): Vertiv and NVIDIA announced joint data-center power/cooling reference designs.
INTC (rival): Intel named as a competitor in NVIDIA 10-K.
ASML (affects NVDA): ASML lithography sets leading-edge capacity at TSMC, which builds NVIDIA's GPUs (indirect).
TSLA (customer): Tesla trains its driving models on large NVIDIA GPU clusters (reported).

mentor.take: On balance: evenly matched. The strongest point for it is analyst forecasts; the biggest worry is the profit cycle. This is a summary of the evidence, not a buy or sell call.

note.headline: NVIDIA holds at 165.05 after 31% jump; fair value still hinges on margins

summary.thesis: NVIDIA's sales and cash flow are growing very fast, and the stock is cheap against its own history, but most of the gap to fair value depends on a record-high profit margin lasting.
summary.decision: Hold for the long term and make no swing trade for now: the price is stuck between support at 147.15–150.45 and heavy resistance at 174.23–180.81.
summary.act_at: Buy at 114.82; go to wait on a close below 147.15; swing entry only on a close above 180.81

note.happening: NVDA closed at 165.05, up 31.48% in a day. It is still in a downtrend, below its 50-day average (206.08) and its 200-day average (202.99). There has been no new news since the last note, and our data has no earnings date.
note.business: The business itself is very strong. Sales over the last twelve months reached 303.0B, up from 165.2B. Growth in the latest quarter sped up to 105.85% from 73.21% two quarters earlier. Operating margin (the share of sales left after running costs) rose to 65.21% from 58.09%. Free cash flow (the cash left after spending on the business) rose to 127.0B from 72.0B, and the company holds 23.2B more cash than debt. Analysts keep raising forecasts: next-year earnings per share (EPS) is now 16.61, up 27.7% in 90 days. Two risks could change the business. First, the margin is at the top of its 5-year range (16–65%), and peaks like that usually fade. Second, unpaid customer bills grew 127% while quarterly sales grew 106%. That can mean sales were pulled forward or customers are paying more slowly. Two other things affect only sentiment or governance, not the business: insiders sold $946.6M outside pre-set trading plans, and the price itself has been extremely volatile. The data has no segment breakdown, so we cannot say which product lines are driving growth.

worth.text: At 165.05, the stock trades at 20.8 times trailing earnings, 17.1 times this year's expected earnings and 9.9 times next year's. Its price-to-sales ratio of 13.1 is just below the peer median of 13.3, and it is at the very bottom (0.0 percentile) of its own 5-year range. The cash-flow model (DCF, which values a company on its future cash) gives 191.49 to 264.22, with 222.58 in the middle. The own-history price-to-sales method gives 217.35 to 411.04. The current price assumes free cash flow starts growing at about 22.0% a year. At 20% starting growth the model value is 152.77, and at 30% it is 222.58. The real swing factor is the margin. If operating margin falls to 48%, the value drops to 114.82, and at 32% it drops to 76.87. Note that the valuation summary text still quotes the old pre-jump price of 125.53.
worth.key_assumption: Operating margin stays near 65.21% instead of fading toward 48%, while free cash flow grows from 127.0B at a starting rate of about 20% or more.
